title: Sharp universal support criterion for sub-Gaussian laws
summary: For every Borel probability law on the real line that is symmetric about zero and satisfies 0 < a <= |X| <= b almost surely, the support ratio b/a <= sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) guarantees E exp(t X) <= exp(t^2 E X^2 / 2) for every real t. The inequality is strict for nonzero t, and the actual variance is the optimal quadratic proxy. An explicit symmetric law on {-R,-1,1,R} violates the bound near zero for each larger ratio R. review.reason: Gives a sharp support-ratio criterion for sub-Gaussian bounds on symmetric laws, with a counterexample.
